text:
Statins are medicines that help lower
your cholesterol.

Cholesterol is a fatty substance
in your blood.
There are two types good, HDL.
And bad, non-HDL cholesterol.

Too much bad cholesterol in your blood
can lead to a buildup

of fatty deposits in the walls
of your arteries, and limit blood flow.
If the arteries become narrow or blocked
it increases your risk of a heart attack or stroke.

Statins help lower the amount of bad
cholesterol your body makes,

and stop more fatty deposits
from building up in your arteries.

This reduces your risk of
a heart attack and stroke.
You should make healthy lifestyle changes

as well as taking a statin
to lower your cholesterol.
Like eating less saturated fat
more fruit and veg
and moving more.

Most people taking
statins don't have any side effects.

However, one side effect
can be muscle pain.

If you're having side effects,
speak to your doctor.

They can help find out what's causing
your symptoms and help you manage them.

For example, they may reduce your dose
or change your statin.

It's important not to stop taking statins
without speaking to your doctor first.

Most people prescribed
a statin will take it every day
for the rest of their life.

It can be difficult to understand why
you need to continue taking your statin
once your cholesterol is lower.
But once you stop taking the statin,

your cholesterol levels
will usually go up again.

Statins are one of the most researched
cardiovascular medicines in the UK.

There's lots of reliable evidence
showing they're safe and effective
for most people.
